newsitem.title: UK: Briton's "bogus defence" in French girl's murder.
newsitem.headline: Briton's "bogus defence" in French girl's murder.

text.p: A British truck driver accused of murdering French teenager Celine Figard has "plainly" confirmed his guilt at the trial, a prosecution lawyer said on Monday.
Stuart Morgan, 37, has denied allegations that he raped, battered and strangled the 19-year-old accountancy student in the back of his lorry cab last December.
He has said in evidence he picked up the hitch-hiker at a motorway service station and they stopped for a sex session in his lorry before he dropped her off at Southampton, south England.
Summing up for the prosecution, lawyer David Farrer said Morgan had presented "a patently bogus defence."
"There are cases in which a guilty man confirms his guilt when he goes into the witness box. This is plainly such a case," he told the jury.
Farrer said Morgan's story was "like a rotten plank which crumbles wherever you touch it."
He said the defendant had changed his story during the trial, denying he had ever made inquiries about buying a new lower bunk for his lorry in the days after Celine went missing.
Morgan is accused of murdering Celine on the lower bunk on December 19, the last day she was seen alive. Her disappearance sparked a massive nationwide police search across Britain.
